newsitem.title: JAPAN: ALPINE SKIING-STREET DREAMS OF RETURNING TO TOP FORM.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-STREET DREAMS OF RETURNING TO TOP FORM.

text.p: World Cup downhill champion Picabo Street, sidelined with a knee injury since December, has been having a recurrent dream that might eventually give her competitors nightmares.

"I'm having dreams of skiing even better than I did before the crash," said the 25-year-old American, who was in Hakuba to cheer on her team mates at a World Cup women's downhill on Friday. "I feel inside that I'm not going to have a problem to get back on my skis.
"I wake up missing skiing though," added Street, who underwent surgery days after tearing ligaments in her left knee during a training run at a World Cup downhill in Vail in the United States.
"I just have to turn that part of me off because there is nothing I can do about it," said Street. "It's a big patience game."
The downhill silver medallist at the 1994 Lillehammer Olympics says she expects to be back on skis by June and in top form by early November.
"My doctor told me when I went to see him at six weeks that I wasn't doing good; I was doing great," she said.
Street even managed a Friday morning inspection trip down the course for next year's Olympics by hitching a ride on a trainer's back with stops en route to examine particular sections.

The course met with her approval. "I think it's going to be a good, challenging course for the Olympics that doesn't favour anyone in particular," she said. "It's got everything -- jumps, turns, flats."

Street is also gathering other vital information to help her in her quest for a medal at the Nagano Games, such as where the American team will stay, where they will eat and whether she will be able to see the race mountain from her window.
"It's amazing what small details make a difference for an athlete," she said.
